parameters.query:
-- Lease a batch of pipeline work. SKIP LOCKED lets several workers tick
-- concurrently without handing the same item to two of them, and the lease_until
-- clause reclaims work abandoned by a worker that died mid-item.
--
-- Redelivery after a lost lease is deliberate: this queue is at-least-once, and
-- correctness comes from the idempotency layer underneath rather than from here.
WITH args AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS a
),
claimable AS (
  SELECT wq.id
  FROM work_queue wq, args
  WHERE wq.kind = 'pipeline'
    AND (
      (wq.state = 'pending' AND wq.run_after <= now())
      OR (wq.state = 'leased' AND wq.lease_until < now())
    )
  ORDER BY wq.run_after, wq.id
  LIMIT COALESCE((SELECT (a->>'batch')::int FROM args), 10)
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
leased AS (
  UPDATE work_queue wq
  SET state = 'leased',
      lease_token = (SELECT a->>'token' FROM args),
      lease_until = now() + (COALESCE((SELECT (a->>'lease_seconds')::int FROM args), 300) * interval '1 second'),
      attempt = wq.attempt + 1,
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE wq.id IN (SELECT id FROM claimable)
  RETURNING wq.*
)
SELECT
  l.id            AS work_id,
  l.lead_id,
  l.attempt,
  l.max_attempts,
  l.payload       AS work_payload,
  to_jsonb(ld.*)  AS lead
FROM leased l
JOIN lead ld ON ld.lead_id = l.lead_id
ORDER BY l.id;

-- Everything the decision step needs, in one round trip: duplicate candidates and
-- the current sales roster with live workload.
--
-- Candidate blocking is exact-match on phone, email, name or company. That is a
-- deliberate simplification: it will miss a typo'd name with no other matching
-- field. Production wants a trigram or phonetic blocking key here; the scoring
-- that follows is unchanged either way.
WITH args AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS a
),
me AS (
  SELECT
    a->>'lead_id'          AS lead_id,
    a->>'phone_e164'       AS phone,
    a->>'email_normalized' AS email,
    a->>'name_normalized'  AS name,
    lower(NULLIF(a->>'company','')) AS company
  FROM args
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(c.*)), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM (
       SELECT l.*
       FROM lead l, me
       WHERE l.lead_id <> me.lead_id
         -- A record already folded into another is not itself a candidate; the
         -- master carries the identity forward.
         AND l.dedup_status <> 'merged_into'
         AND (
           (me.phone   IS NOT NULL AND l.phone_e164      = me.phone)
           OR (me.email   IS NOT NULL AND l.email_normalized = me.email)
           OR (me.name    IS NOT NULL AND l.name_normalized  = me.name)
           OR (me.company IS NOT NULL AND lower(l.company)   = me.company)
         )
       ORDER BY l.ingested_at DESC
       LIMIT 50
     ) c
  ) AS candidates,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r.*) ORDER BY r.open_leads::float / GREATEST(r.capacity,1)), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM sales_rep r
     WHERE NOT r.is_manager
  ) AS reps,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(m.*)), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM sales_rep m WHERE m.is_manager AND m.available
  ) AS managers;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ JSON.stringify({ lead_id: $json.lead.lead_id, phone_e164: $json.lead.phone_e164, email_normalized: $json.lead.email_normalized, name_normalized: $json.lead.name_normalized, company: $json.lead.company }) ] }}

parameters.query:
-- Commit every decision the pipeline made, in one statement.
--
-- The version predicate on the lead update is the entity-level compare-and-set.
-- If another workflow wrote this lead while we were deciding, zero rows update and
-- every dependent CTE produces nothing — no partial application. The work item then
-- stays leased, expires, and is retried against fresh state.
WITH args AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS a
),
d AS (
  SELECT
    a                       AS root,
    a->'decision'           AS dec,
    a->>'lead_id'           AS lead_id,
    (a->>'expected_version')::int AS expected_version
  FROM args
),
updated AS (
  UPDATE lead l SET
    enrichment          = COALESCE(d.dec->'enrichment', l.enrichment),
    score               = NULLIF(d.dec->>'score','')::int,
    score_breakdown     = COALESCE(d.dec->'score_breakdown', l.score_breakdown),
    score_model_version = NULLIF(d.dec->>'score_model_version',''),
    score_band          = NULLIF(d.dec->>'score_band',''),
    ai_classification   = d.dec->'ai_classification',
    conflict_flag       = COALESCE((d.dec->>'conflict_flag')::boolean, false),
    disposition         = NULLIF(d.dec->>'disposition',''),
    owner_id            = NULLIF(d.dec->>'owner_id',''),
    assignment_reason   = NULLIF(d.dec->>'assignment_reason',''),
    assigned_at         = CASE WHEN NULLIF(d.dec->>'owner_id','') IS NOT NULL THEN now() ELSE l.assigned_at END,
    vip_flag            = COALESCE((d.dec->>'vip')::boolean, false),
    approval_state      = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.dec->>'approval_state',''), l.approval_state),
    dedup_status        = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.dec->>'dedup_status',''), l.dedup_status),
    duplicate_of        = NULLIF(d.dec->>'duplicate_of',''),
    dedup_confidence    = NULLIF(d.dec->>'dedup_confidence','')::numeric,
    dedup_features      = d.dec->'dedup_features',
    status              = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.dec->>'status',''), l.status),
    status_reason       = NULLIF(d.dec->>'status_reason',''),
    version             = l.version + 1,
    updated_at          = now()
  FROM d
  WHERE l.lead_id = d.lead_id
    AND l.version = d.expected_version
    -- A deferred item made no decision to commit; it only needs rescheduling.
    AND COALESCE(d.root->>'defer','false') <> 'true'
  RETURNING l.lead_id, l.version, l.owner_id, l.disposition
),
-- Retryable upstream failure: hand the item back to the queue with backoff rather
-- than committing a decision made on data we could not fetch (edge case 3).
deferred AS (
  UPDATE work_queue w
  SET state = 'pending',
      run_after = now() + (COALESCE((d.root->>'retry_after_seconds')::numeric, 5) * interval '1 second'),
      lease_token = NULL,
      lease_until = NULL,
      last_error = d.root->'defer_reason',
      updated_at = now()
  FROM d
  WHERE w.id = (d.root->>'work_id')::bigint
    AND COALESCE(d.root->>'defer','false') = 'true'
  RETURNING w.id, w.attempt, w.run_after
),
defer_audit AS (
  INSERT INTO event_log (lead_id, workflow, execution_id, step, event_type, decision, inputs, outputs, severity)
  SELECT d.lead_id, d.root->>'workflow', d.root->>'execution_id', 'enrich', 'work.deferred', 'retry',
         jsonb_build_object('attempt', df.attempt), 
         jsonb_build_object('retry_after', df.run_after, 'reason', d.root->'defer_reason'),
         'warn'
  FROM deferred df, d
  RETURNING id
),
-- Every candidate assessed, not just the winner, so a threshold can be re-argued
-- later from what was actually seen.
dedup_written AS (
  INSERT INTO duplicate_decision
    (lead_id, candidate_lead_id, confidence, features, tier, action_taken, demoted_reason)
  SELECT
    u.lead_id,
    c->>'candidate_lead_id',
    (c->>'confidence')::numeric,
    c->'features',
    c->>'tier',
    c->>'action_taken',
    NULLIF(c->>'demoted_reason','')
  FROM updated u, d, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(d.dec->'dedup_decisions','[]'::jsonb)) c
  RETURNING id
),
-- The surviving record is marked as a master. Deliberately does not bump its
-- version: this is metadata about the merge, and bumping it would make a
-- concurrent pipeline run on the master fail its own compare-and-set.
master_marked AS (
  UPDATE lead m SET dedup_status = 'master', updated_at = now()
  FROM updated u, d
  WHERE m.lead_id = NULLIF(d.dec->>'duplicate_of','')
    AND m.dedup_status <> 'merged_into'
  RETURNING m.lead_id
),
audit AS (
  INSERT INTO event_log
    (lead_id, workflow, execution_id, step, event_type, decision, inputs, outputs, idempotency_key, severity)
  SELECT
    u.lead_id,
    d.root->>'workflow',
    d.root->>'execution_id',
    e->>'step',
    e->>'event_type',
    e->>'decision',
    e->'inputs',
    e->'outputs',
    NULLIF(e->>'idempotency_key',''),
    COALESCE(NULLIF(e->>'severity',''), 'info')
  FROM updated u, d, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(d.dec->'events','[]'::jsonb)) e
  RETURNING id
),
-- The token is generated here rather than in a Code node: it goes in a callback
-- URL, so it has to be unguessable, and the sandbox has no CSPRNG.
approval AS (
  INSERT INTO approval_request (lead_id, kind, state, token, expires_at)
  SELECT u.lead_id, 'vip', 'pending', gen_random_uuid()::text,
         now() + (COALESCE((d.dec->>'approval_timeout_minutes')::int, 30) * interval '1 minute')
  FROM updated u, d
  WHERE (d.dec->>'approval_required')::boolean IS TRUE
  RETURNING id, token
),
-- Downstream side effects are enqueued, never performed here. wf-10 therefore has
-- no external effects of its own beyond two reads, which is what makes it safe to
-- replay wholesale.
enqueued AS (
  INSERT INTO work_queue (kind, lead_id, payload, idempotency_key, run_after, max_attempts)
  SELECT
    q->>'kind',
    u.lead_id,
    COALESCE(q->'payload','{}'::jsonb),
    NULLIF(q->>'idempotency_key',''),
    now() + (COALESCE((q->>'delay_seconds')::int, 0) * interval '1 second'),
    COALESCE((q->>'max_attempts')::int, 5)
  FROM updated u, d, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(d.dec->'enqueue','[]'::jsonb)) q
  RETURNING id
),
workload AS (
  UPDATE sales_rep r
  SET open_leads = r.open_leads + 1, updated_at = now()
  FROM updated u
  WHERE r.rep_id = u.owner_id
    AND (SELECT dec->>'owner_changed' FROM d) = 'true'
  RETURNING r.rep_id, r.open_leads
),
finished AS (
  UPDATE work_queue w
  SET state = 'done', lease_token = NULL, lease_until = NULL, updated_at = now()
  FROM d
  WHERE w.id = (d.root->>'work_id')::bigint
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM updated)
  RETURNING w.id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM updated)       AS lead_updated,
  (SELECT lead_id FROM updated)             AS lead_id,
  (SELECT disposition FROM updated)         AS disposition,
  (SELECT owner_id FROM updated)            AS owner_id,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM dedup_written) AS dedup_rows,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM audit)         AS audit_rows,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM enqueued)      AS enqueued_rows,
  (SELECT token FROM approval)              AS approval_token,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM finished)      AS work_completed,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM master_marked) AS master_marked,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM deferred)      AS deferred;

parameters.content:
## The pipeline — every decision, no side effects
Dedup, enrichment, scoring, AI classification, routing and assignment.

**This workflow performs no external writes.** Its only outbound calls are two reads. Everything side-effecting is *enqueued* for the dispatcher that owns it — which is precisely what makes the whole pipeline safe to re-run (**edge case 14**).

### The AI is an untrusted service
Responses are requested as **text, not JSON**, so a malformed body is ours to inspect rather than a node crash.

Empty, truncated and unparseable all degrade to score-only with a stated reason (**edge case 4**). The model never feeds the score — it produces an independent label, and disagreement is a *routing* signal (**edge case 5**).

### One statement commits everything
Lead update, dedup decisions, audit rows, approval request, downstream queue items and work completion.

The `version` predicate is the compare-and-set: if another workflow wrote this lead while we were deciding, **zero rows update and every dependent CTE produces nothing**. No partial application.

### Retry lives in the queue
A retryable enrichment failure hands the item back with full-jitter backoff (**edge case 3**).

Once attempts are spent the lead proceeds degraded — a provider that is down must not hold a lead hostage forever.
